real_estate.homebuilder: The 30-year reached 7.50%, its highest since April 2024, and rental investors are pulling back.
real_estate.commentary:
Mortgage rates set another high for the year. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year rose to 7.50% on Monday, the highest since April 2024, and the 15-year reached 7.12%, while the 10-Year Treasury closed at 5.24%, its highest close since June 2007. The 30-year started September at 6.89%; on our five city median of $1,090,000 with 20% down, that climb adds about $360 a month.

Rental investors are stepping back. In a ResiClub and LendingOne survey of 216 single-family landlords taken August 17 to September 14, 65% expect the 30-year to average above 6.5% over the next year, up from 11% in late 2025, and 44% say they are unlikely to buy another rental in the next 12 months, the most in the survey's two years.

Insurance is part of it: 84% say rising premiums cut into their cash flow. The newsletter wrote that 59% plan 1% to 3% rent hikes; in the survey, 59% plan an increase of some size and 31% expect 1% to 3%.

Locally, the five city ledger dipped to 703 from 717 on Monday, with Milpitas down six, and the board wide table fell 35 to 2,727. For the record, UBS's annual bubble index, out last week, files San Francisco under low risk; Zurich and Tokyo are the only high risk cities of the 23 it tracks.

What this means for you: with fewer investors planning purchases, buyers who can carry today's payment may find less competition. Sellers should price for 7.5% money; 163 of the ledger's 617 homes on the market have been listed 60 days or longer.

• Board wide: 2,727 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 179 coming soon and 212 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 703 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 617 are on the market and 86 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 254 live, 197 active, 33 coming soon, 24 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,199,990 at $769 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 29 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 180, Milpitas 115, Newark 88, Union City 66.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,090,000 at $675 a square foot. 283 homes are priced under a million, and 163 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

stocks.news:
Stocks slipped Monday as the 10-Year climbed to its highest close since 2007, and Tuesday is a little softer so far. The day's two biggest company stories both start in the Bay Area.

Nvidia is the first chart. Its board approved another $150 billion for buybacks on Monday, which the company calls the largest authorization increase in history, lifting what it has left to spend to $235 billion through fiscal 2028. That tops Apple's $110 billion from 2024, the largest single U.S. authorization until now, and it is the Santa Clara company's third increase in 13 months. The stock rose 1.68% Monday to $228.86.

Anthropic is the second. Reuters reported Monday that the San Francisco company's draft IPO prospectus, filed confidentially and not yet public, shows a $42 billion net loss for 2025 on revenue that grew 12-fold to nearly $4.6 billion; about $34 billion of that loss was a non-cash accounting charge tied to its financing, and the operating loss was $8.06 billion, up from $2.98 billion in 2024. Reuters says the offering could value the company at more than $2 trillion, and Anthropic has committed at least $518 billion to computing capacity over about a decade.

feature_images.alt: Horizontal bar chart of the largest single share buyback authorization by each U.S. company: Nvidia $150 billion in September 2026, Apple $110 billion in May 2024, Chevron $75 billion in January 2023, Alphabet $70 billion each April from 2022 to 2025, and Microsoft $60 billion in September 2021 and 2024.
feature_images.caption: Nvidia's $150 billion authorization is the largest single one on record, ahead of Apple's $110 billion in 2024. One bar per company; Apple alone has authorized $90 billion or more seven times.
feature_images.source: Source: NVIDIA release, September 28, 2026; Apple, Chevron, Alphabet and Microsoft releases and SEC filings.

feature_images.alt: Horizontal waterfall chart of Anthropic's 2025 results as reported by Reuters from its draft IPO prospectus: revenue of about $4.6 billion, minus $7.33 billion for compute and infrastructure and $5.32 billion of other operating costs, gives an operating loss of $8.06 billion, against $2.98 billion in 2024. An accounting charge on financing of about $34 billion, not cash spent, brings the net loss to $42 billion. A note adds at least $518 billion of computing commitments over about a decade.
feature_images.caption: Most of Anthropic's $42 billion 2025 loss was a non-cash accounting charge on its financing; the operating loss was $8.06 billion on revenue of nearly $4.6 billion, per Reuters.
feature_images.source: Source: Reuters, September 28 and 29, 2026, reporting Anthropic's confidential draft registration statement.

economy.note: All four are Monday, September 28: the Treasury daily yield curve close, the COMEX December gold and silver settlements, and the ICE November Brent settlement. Tuesday is live: at 8:35 AM PT the 10-Year was near 5.27%, gold $4,188.00 (+0.47%), silver $61.25 (-0.77%) and Brent $104.41 (-0.83%).
economy.commentary:
Rising yields hit metals hard on Monday: December gold settled down 3.54% and silver 4.76%. The newsletter printed gold at down 0.01%; its level was right, the change was not. Gold is bouncing this morning.

Oil's round trip is back on. Brent's front month averaged $65 a barrel in January, $104 in May and $85 in July, and September is back to $102 so far. The November contract settled at $105.28 Monday after Bloomberg reported that Iranian officials see little chance of a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz before November.

The version of this chart making the rounds joins eight months of physical spot averages to one day's futures price; ours keeps every month on the contract we quote. Closer to home, San Francisco regular gas averaged $6.27 a gallon Monday, past May's peak and $1.84 above a year ago, per the EIA, while the national average slipped to $4.47. Bay Area pumps made the round trip too, and came back higher.

feature_image.alt: Line chart of Brent crude front month futures, monthly average settlement per barrel in 2026: January $65, February $69, March $100, April $102, May $104 (the year's high), June $85, July $85, August $88, and September 1 to 28 $102, with Monday's settle at $105.28. Shaded bars show each month's lowest to highest daily settlement.
feature_image.caption: Brent's monthly average went from $65 in January to $104 in May, fell to $85 by July, and is back to $102 in September. Every month is on the futures contract quoted in our Economy section.
feature_image.source: Source: ICE Futures Europe via Yahoo Finance (Brent front month, November contract for September); U.S. EIA Europe Brent spot for the comparison.

crypto.commentary:
Crypto is mixed this morning. Bitcoin is at $83,130, down 0.26% over 24 hours and up about a third since mid-August; Ether is up 0.14% and XRP up 1.49%. Prices are live from Coinbase at 8:35 AM PT.

Citi and Coinbase said Monday that merchants using Spring by Citi will be able to take stablecoin payments at checkout, converted to dollars automatically with Citi settling as the bank of record. Separately, Bloomberg reports Blockchain.com is telling investors it wants to list this year, raising about $500 million at a $4 billion to $6 billion valuation.
